title: Move logic into services
idea: A service is a module of plain functions that holds your rules and queries. It knows nothing about HTTP, so controllers can stay thin.
points: The controller reads `req`, picks the status code and calls `res.json`.
`createUser` hashes and inserts, then returns a user or `null`. It never sees `req`.
`auth.validation.js` holds only Zod schemas that controllers and tests can share.
The refactor moves code. The requests and responses stay exactly the same.

hero.title: Who does what after the refactor

edges.caption: The route only maps `POST /auth/signup` to a controller function.

edges.caption: The controller asks the schema to check the body. A failure becomes a 400.

edges.label: createUser
edges.caption: Valid data goes to the service as plain arguments. No `req` or `res` crosses this line.

edges.label: insert
edges.caption: The service hashes the password and runs the query.

edges.label: user or null
edges.caption: The service returns data. The controller turns it into 201 or 409.

code.title: Three small modules
code.caption: Each `// src/...` block is its own file in the project, with `import` lines added. One file here, so it runs alone.

walk.text: Validation module: only Zod schemas, reusable by controllers and tests.
Service: hash, then insert. Plain values in, a row out. No `req`, no `res`.
A duplicate gives no row, so the service returns `null`. It does not pick a status code.
Controller: shape the 400 body. This is HTTP work, so it stays here.
The handler is short: validate, call the service, map the result to 201 or 409.
The same requests as before give the same answers.
The service also works with no HTTP at all, so a script or a test can reuse it.

pitfalls: Keep `req`, `res` and status codes out of services. Pass values in; return values out.
After moving code, re-run the requests. Check 201, 400 and 409 still come back.

quiz.why: On a duplicate, `onConflictDoNothing()` returns no row, so the service returns `null`. The controller turns that into 409.

takeaway: Controllers speak HTTP; services do the work and know nothing of it.
